events.title: Birth of Benjamin Franklin
events.description: Benjamin Franklin was born in Boston. He grew up to be a printer, writer, scientist and inventor. He was also one of the Founding Fathers of the United States.
events.significance: Franklin's electrical experiments, his diplomacy in France during the American Revolution, and his role in drafting the nation's founding documents made him one of the most influential figures in American history.

events.title: Captain Cook Crosses the Antarctic Circle
events.description: Captain James Cook, commanding HMS Resolution on his second voyage, became the first known person to cross the Antarctic Circle.
events.significance: The crossing marked a milestone in polar exploration. Cook's voyage helped disprove the idea of a habitable southern continent in temperate latitudes.

events.title: United States Buys the Virgin Islands
events.description: The United States paid Denmark $25 million for the Danish West Indies, which became the U.S. Virgin Islands.
events.significance: The purchase gave the U.S. a strategic Caribbean position near the Panama Canal. It also added a lasting overseas territory.

events.title: Patrice Lumumba Is Murdered
events.description: Patrice Lumumba, the first democratically elected prime minister of the Congo, was killed after being deposed and detained. Western governments supported the plot.
events.significance: His death became a symbol of Cold War interference in newly independent African nations. It also shaped the Congo's turbulent decades that followed.

events.title: The Gulf War Begins
events.description: A U.S.-led coalition launched Operation Desert Storm with a massive air campaign against Iraq. The aim was to force Iraqi troops out of Kuwait.
events.significance: The war showed modern precision air power and live global television coverage. It also reshaped Middle Eastern politics and U.S. foreign policy.
